short: The finitistic dimension can be infinite

title.title: The finitistic dimension conjecture fails
title.subtitle: Claim: a finite-dimensional algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ with modules of finite but unbounded projective dimension

plain: One fixed algebra has modules whose 'unwinding' takes finitely many steps, but as many as you like

beats.text: One fixed algebra $A$, and for every $m$ a module $N_m$
Each $N_m$ has finite projective dimension, at least $2m-2$
No finite bound fits them all: the finitistic dimension of $A$ is $\infty$

steps: Apply one fixed operation F to the module, again and again
It survives $2m-2$ rounds, so the resolution is at least that long
It dies after $2m$ rounds, so the resolution is finite

achievement.label: Bass's finitistic dimension conjecture (1960)
achievement.context: Before: monomial and radical-cube-zero algebras, representation dimension at most 3 (Igusa–Todorov)
achievement.note: Also an algebra with finitistic dimension infinite on the left, 0 on the right

verify.detail: Lean defines the little finitistic dimension with Mathlib's projectiveDimension and asks for this
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not run the checker

voice.text: Bass expected finite resolutions to have bounded length; here they grow without bound.
One operation, repeated, dies after two m rounds but not two m minus two.
Claimed: the finitistic dimension is infinite.
